name: Brown's Hotel London
insider_take: London's first hotel continues to set the standard for timeless British elegance in the heart of Mayfair.
whats_special: Brown's Hotel holds the prestigious title of London's first hotel, opening in 1837. This historic Mayfair property is where afternoon tea was first served in a hotel, and it's been perfected here for over 180 years. The hotel occupies 11 Georgian townhouses seamlessly connected, creating an intimate village-like atmosphere in central London. Notable guests have included Theodore Roosevelt, Agatha Christie (who wrote parts of her novels here), and Queen Victoria's son.
pro_tip: Book the legendary afternoon tea at least 6 weeks in advance - it's served in the same drawing room where the tradition began, complete with finger sandwiches, scones, and pastries on fine bone china.
dont_miss: The English Tea Room for the original afternoon tea experience, HIX Mayfair restaurant featuring British cuisine, and the hotel's prime location just steps from Bond Street shopping, Green Park, and the Royal Academy of Arts. The cozy Donovan Bar serves vintage cocktails in an intimate setting lined with photographs by Terence Donovan.
pros: Historic luxury hotel with exceptional British heritage and traditional afternoon tea
Prime Mayfair location with easy access to Bond Street shopping and major attractions
Impeccable service and attention to detail from highly trained staff
Elegant rooms and suites with classic English décor and modern amenities
cons: Premium pricing reflective of luxury Mayfair location
Traditional décor may feel dated to some modern travelers
